title: Attachment Sandboxing
summary: Attachment sandboxing is an email security control that executes or opens a suspicious attachment in an isolated, instrumented environment before the message is delivered, then decides based on observed behaviour rather than on a signature. A typical pipeline detonates the file in a virtual machine, records process creation, file and registry writes, persistence attempts and outbound network connections, and produces a verdict the mail gateway uses to block, quarantine, strip or deliver the message. Because judgement is behavioural, sandboxing can catch new malware and document exploits that no signature matches yet, and it gives analysts artefacts to review. It is also inherently evadable: samples that sleep past the analysis window, detect a virtual machine, require a specific date, a valid recipient reply or user interaction may look harmless and be delivered. The mistake is treating a sandbox as a complete answer; it works best alongside restrictions on executable and macro attachments, script and macro blocking in the mail client, link isolation and a strong user reporting habit.

beginner.definition: Attachment sandboxing is a way to check email attachments safely. A sandbox is an isolated computer with no real data on it. A suspicious file is opened there first. Someone watches what the file tries to do before the email reaches you.
beginner.whyItMatters: Most malware arrives as an attachment or a link inside email. Signature based tools only know malware they have already seen. A sandbox judges behaviour instead, so it can catch brand new files. It also gives the mail system a clear reason to block a message. Users should still be careful, because a clever file can hide.
howItWorks: An email arrives at the mail gateway with a document attached to it.
The gateway copies the file into a locked and isolated test machine.
The sandbox opens the file and records every action the file takes.
The system looks for strange behaviour, such as contacting an outside server.
The gateway then blocks, quarantines or delivers the message based on that.
Skilled attackers can make a file wait or hide, so a clean result is not proof.
beginner.example: Think of a post room that receives a strange parcel. Staff do not open it at their own desk. They carry it to a sealed room and watch it through a window. If it beeps, smokes or starts a timer, the whole delivery is refused. The sealed room is the sandbox, and it never touches the real office.
takeaways: A sandbox judges behaviour, so it can catch malware with no known signature.
Clever files can delay or hide, so a clean verdict is not a guarantee.
Combine sandboxing with attachment type limits and user reporting.

objectives: Explain what attachment sandboxing does and where it sits in the mail path.
Describe the behaviours a sandbox watches for when it detonates a file.
Explain how the verdict from a sandbox changes what happens to a message.
Recognise the evasion techniques that limit sandbox reliability.
List the additional email controls that support sandboxing.
